author: massicomar
title: Longest Path
summary:
There is a directed graph $G$ with $N$ vertices and $M$ edges. The vertices are numbered $1, 2, \ldots, N$, and for each $i$ ($1 \leq i \leq M$), the $i$-th directed edge goes from Vertex $x_i$ to $y_i$. $G$ does not contain directed cycles.

Find the length of the longest directed path in $G$. Here, the length of a directed path is the number of edges in it.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

$N$ $M$
$x_1$ $y_1$
$x_2$ $y_2$
$:$
$x_M$ $y_M$

Output

Print the length of the longest directed path in $G$.
explanation: Longest path is NP-hard in general but easy on a DAG: process vertices in topological order (or memoized DFS).
traps: Running Dijkstra with negated weights is wrong (negative edges).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[v] = length of the longest path starting at v
dp[mask][v] = longest path visiting exactly the set mask ending at v
options.why: That's for general graphs (Hamiltonian-style); a DAG doesn't need it, and N = 1e5.

options.text: dp[k] = whether a path of length k exists

options.why: Asks for the longest path over all starts, not a shortest path.

options.text: dp[v] = length of the longest path ending at v

extraLayers.explanation: Because there are no cycles, the best path from v only depends on the best paths from its out-neighbours. (Ending at v works too.)

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[v] = max over edges v→u of dp[u] + 1, computed in reverse topological order (or memoized DFS)
dp[v] = max over edges v→u of dp[u] + 1, computed in increasing vertex index
options.why: Vertex numbers aren't a topological order.

options.text: Relax edges with a priority queue keyed by −length

extraLayers.explanation: Evaluate a vertex only after all its successors — exactly what topological order guarantees.

es.explanation: El camino más largo es NP-difícil en general, pero fácil en un DAG: procesa los vértices en orden topológico (o con un DFS memoizado).
traps: Correr Dijkstra con los pesos negados está mal (aristas negativas).

dp-state.explanation: Como no hay ciclos, el mejor camino desde v solo depende de los mejores caminos desde sus vecinos de salida. (Terminar en v también sirve.)

why.b: Eso es para grafos generales (tipo hamiltoniano); un DAG no lo necesita, y N = 1e5.
why.d: Se pide el camino más largo entre todos los inicios, no un camino mínimo.

dp-transition.explanation: Evalúa un vértice recién después de todos sus sucesores: justo lo que garantiza el orden topológico.

why.b: Los números de los vértices no son un orden topológico.
why.c: El invariante de Dijkstra se rompe con pesos de “más largo” (negativos).
why.d: Cuenta el grado, no el largo del camino.
